intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Explore the stunning Phi Phi archipelago by longtail boat, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, visiting Monkey Beach, and swimming through vibrant coral reefs. A full-day guided tour covering multiple islands with snorkeling gear included.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Bangkok's legendary street food scene at Yaowarat Road (Chinatown), sampling pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh seafood. Join a guided walking tour or explore independently through the bustling night stalls.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Sunset Beach Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle a sea kayak along Koh Lanta's serene coastline, exploring hidden sea caves, mangrove tunnels, and secluded beaches. Watch the spectacular Andaman Sea sunset from the water before returning to shore for fresh grilled fish at a beachside shack.
experiences.location: Klong Dao Beach, Koh Lanta, Krabi Province

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Cooking Class & Morning Market Visit
experiences.description: Start at a local fresh market to handpick ingredients, then learn to prepare 5 authentic Northern Thai dishes including khao soi, green curry, and som tum. Hosted at a traditional Thai house with a garden herb walk included.

experiences.name: Similan Islands Liveaboard Snorkel Day Trip
experiences.description: Board a speedboat to the world-renowned Similan Islands, one of Thailand's top diving and snorkeling destinations. Explore multiple dive sites teeming with manta rays, whale sharks, and colorful reef fish, with lunch and equipment provided on this full-day excursion.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, exchange currency at the airport (avoid hotel exchange desks for better rates). Take a budget shuttle or shared minivan toward the pier for Phi Phi Islands. If time allows, grab a quick bite near the pier area at Rassada Pier or Ao Nang.
day_by_day.evening: Board the late afternoon ferry to Phi Phi Don Island (ferries typically run until ~17:00 from Phuket or Krabi). Arrive at Phi Phi Don, check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a slow evening stroll along Tonsai Village's main walking street to get oriented.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip
meals.lunch: Quick street food near the pier — Pad Thai or Khao Man Gai from a local stall (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village night market — try grilled skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh fruit shakes (~150–200 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance online to save time. Carry small Thai baht bills for street food vendors. October is shoulder/wet season — expect occasional rain showers but fewer crowds and lower prices.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to Phi Phi Viewpoint (free entry, ~20-minute uphill walk from Tonsai). Catch panoramic views of both Tonsai Bay and Loh Dalum Bay at sunrise — one of the most iconic sights in Thailand. Bring water and wear good shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget snorkeling longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Leh, including Maya Bay, Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave (~400–600 THB per person for shared group tours booked locally). Swim in crystal-clear turquoise water and explore the famous filming location of 'The Beach'.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and explore the beachfront bars along Loh Dalum Bay. Watch the sunset from the beach. Enjoy a laid-back evening with cheap Chang beer (~60 THB) from a convenience store and sit on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancake and fresh fruit shake from a street stall in Tonsai (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat on the boat tour — buy fresh coconut and fruit from pier vendors (~50 THB)
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant in Tonsai — Green curry with rice and a Thai iced tea (~180–220 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book snorkeling tours directly from local operators on the island rather than through hotel desks to get better prices. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect coral reefs.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak (~200–300 THB/hour) and paddle around the quieter eastern side of Phi Phi Don toward Loh Bakao Bay. Explore hidden coves and mangroves at your own pace. Alternatively, walk to the quieter Long Beach (Hat Yao) on the southeastern side of the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai), a tiny uninhabited island with powdery white sand and shallow turquoise water (~300–400 THB return, shared boat). Snorkel, sunbathe, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere away from the main tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Back on Phi Phi Don, visit the local fresh market near the pier for cheap eats. Try som tam (papaya salad), grilled corn, and fresh coconut ice cream. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the guesthouse or join a fire show on Loh Dalum Beach (free to watch).

meals.breakfast: Congee (rice porridge) or toast with eggs from a local breakfast shop (~70–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Bring packed snacks to Bamboo Island or eat at a simple beach shack (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Fresh market near the pier — mix of street food dishes (~150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate longtail boat prices — group sharing is always cheaper. Bamboo Island is best visited on weekdays when it's less crowded. Bring your own drinking water to avoid buying expensive bottles on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (~200–250 THB, 1.5 hours). Check into a budget guesthouse in Krabi Town near Chao Fah Pier. Drop your bags and head to the famous Krabi Town Walking Street Market if it's a weekend, or explore the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking 360-degree views over Krabi's limestone karsts and jungle (free entry, donations welcome). The climb takes about 45 minutes each way — bring water.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's vibrant night market (Maharaj Market) along the riverside. Sample an enormous variety of cheap Thai street food — satay skewers, pad see ew, rotee with banana and condensed milk, and fresh fruit.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the ferry or grab a quick bite at the Phi Phi pier before departure (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Simple rice and curry at a local Krabi Town restaurant — choose from a display of pre-cooked dishes (~70–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town night market — budget feast for ~150–200 THB with multiple dishes and desserts

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous but very rewarding. Wear modest clothing as it's a religious site. Krabi Town is significantly cheaper than the islands for accommodation and food — a great day to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Take a 45-minute songthaew (shared red truck taxi, ~50 THB) to Ao Nang Beach. Walk along the beachfront promenade and explore the shops and cafes. Rent a beach chair and enjoy the dramatic limestone karst scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Book a shared longtail boat tour from Ao Nang to the Four Islands (Koh Poda, Koh Gai/Chicken Island, Koh Tub, and Koh Mor) — ~500–700 THB for a half-day shared tour. Snorkel, swim, and walk across the sandbars connecting the islands at low tide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang for sunset views. Browse the Ao Nang night market for dinner. Try fresh grilled seafood at budget prices — whole grilled fish, prawns, and squid with sticky rice.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie bowl or toast from a cafe in Krabi Town before heading out (~100 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at a beach shack on one of the Four Islands (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang night market — grilled seafood platter and iced Thai tea (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The sandbar walk between Koh Tub and Koh Mor is tide-dependent — check tide times before booking. Book Four Islands tours directly at the Ao Nang pier for the best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (~100 THB, 15 minutes) — only accessible by boat due to towering cliffs. Explore East Railay and West Railay beaches. Hike to the Railay Viewpoint through the jungle for panoramic karst views (free, ~30-minute hike).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Phra Nang Cave Beach, one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches with a dramatic cave shrine. Snorkel in the clear water or simply relax on the white sand. Explore the Diamond Cave (Tham Phra Nang Nai) with its sparkling stalactites (~200 THB entry).
day_by_day.evening: Catch the longtail boat back to Ao Nang before dark. Return to Krabi Town for a final budget dinner. Pack your bags for the next destination.

meals.breakfast: Khao Tom (Thai rice soup) from a local Krabi Town breakfast stall (~60 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant on Railay — slightly pricier due to location, but affordable set meals available (~180–220 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town local restaurant — Massaman curry with roti bread (~150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach has no ATMs — bring enough cash before heading over. West Railay Beach is the prettier and more swimmable side. Longtail boats run frequently but confirm the last departure time back to Ao Nang.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus or minivan from Krabi to Koh Lanta (~250–300 THB, 2 hours including ferry crossing). Check into a budget bungalow on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao). Walk along the long, peaceful beach and enjoy the more relaxed, less touristy atmosphere of Koh Lanta.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a motorbike (~200–300 THB/day) and explore the island at your own pace. Visit Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) on the eastern coast — a charming historic fishing village with Chinese-Malay wooden shophouses on stilts over the water. Browse local craft shops and cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the southern tip of the island to Mu Ko Lanta National Park for sunset views over the Andaman Sea from the lighthouse (~200 THB park entry). Return to Long Beach for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Krabi Town — roti canai with curry dipping sauce (~60 THB)
meals.lunch: Simple seafood restaurant in Koh Lanta Old Town — fried rice with prawns (~120 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant on Long Beach — Tom Yum soup and grilled fish (~200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is significantly less crowded than Phi Phi or Krabi, making it ideal for a relaxed day. Motorbike rental is the best way to explore — traffic is light and roads are good. October may bring some rain but the island is still beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Ride your rented motorbike to Khlong Nin Beach and Khlong Hin Beach on the western coast — quieter and more secluded than Long Beach. Swim and snorkel in the calm waters. The rocky headlands between beaches offer great snorkeling spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Thung Yee Pheng mangrove forest near the northern part of the island. Take a short kayak or boat tour through the mangroves (~300 THB) to spot wildlife. Alternatively, visit Khlong Jark Waterfall in the national park — a short jungle hike to a refreshing waterfall.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach for a final Koh Lanta sunset. Enjoy dinner at one of the casual beachfront restaurants. Prepare for the next day's journey.

meals.breakfast: Fruit pancakes and coffee from a beach cafe on Long Beach (~100 THB)
meals.lunch: Local Thai restaurant near Khlong Nin Beach — Pad Kra Pao (basil stir fry) with egg on rice (~100 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront BBQ restaurant on Long Beach — grilled squid and sticky rice (~180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Fill up the motorbike before exploring — fuel stations can be sparse in the south. Bring cash as many local restaurants and shops on Koh Lanta don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Krabi by minivan/ferry early morning. From Krabi, take a bus or minivan northward to Khao Sok National Park (~300–400 THB, 3 hours). Check into a budget treehouse bungalow or riverside guesthouse near the park entrance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Khao Sok village strip and book activities for the next day. Take a self-guided walk along the short nature trail near the park entrance to spot wildlife and massive Rafflesia flowers (seasonal). Swim in the Sok River near your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a peaceful evening in the jungle — listen to the sounds of the rainforest. Dine at one of the simple local restaurants in Khao Sok village.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Krabi bus terminal before departure (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Eat on the road or at a roadside stop — simple Thai noodle soup (~70 THB)
meals.dinner: Khao Sok village restaurant — jungle curry (Gaeng Pa) with rice (~150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Khao Sok is one of the world's oldest rainforests and a dramatic contrast to the beaches. October is the wet season here — pack a light rain jacket. Book any national park activities (boat tours, night safaris) in advance or upon arrival at your guesthouse.

day_by_day.morning: Join an early morning guided jungle trek through Khao Sok National Park (~400–600 THB for a shared guided tour). Spot exotic wildlife including hornbills, macaques, gibbons, and exotic plants. Trek to hidden waterfalls deep in the jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat tour on the stunning Cheow Lan Lake (Ratchaprapha Dam) — a vast emerald lake surrounded by towering limestone karsts (~600–800 THB for a shared day tour). Swim in the warm lake water and explore floating raft houses.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Khao Sok village by late afternoon. Relax at the riverside with a cold drink. Enjoy a final dinner in the village before preparing to head south.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — eggs, toast, and fruit (~100 THB) or included with accommodation
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included with most guided tours, or eat at a lakeside floating restaurant (~150 THB)
meals.dinner: Khao Sok village — mixed Thai dishes and fresh juices (~180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Cheow Lan Lake is one of Thailand's most spectacular and underrated sights. The floating raft houses on the lake are a unique accommodation option if you want to spend a night on the water (book in advance). Leeches may be present on jungle trails — wear covered shoes and socks.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early minivan from Khao Sok back toward the coast, heading to Koh Samui or Surat Thani pier (~300 THB). Board a ferry to Koh Tao (~600–700 THB, 3–4 hours) — Thailand's legendary diving and snorkeling island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Tao, check into a budget dive resort or guesthouse in Mae Haad or Sairee Beach. Explore Sairee Beach — the main beach strip with a lively but relaxed atmosphere. Rent a snorkel set (~100 THB/day) and snorkel directly from the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sairee Beach strip and explore the affordable restaurants and bars. Watch the sunset from the beach. Enjoy a casual dinner at one of the many budget-friendly restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure at Khao Sok or on the minivan stop (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Simple noodle soup or fried rice at Koh Tao pier upon arrival (~80 THB)
meals.dinner: Sairee Beach restaurant — Pad Thai with tofu or chicken and Chang beer (~180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Tao is one of the world's best and most affordable places to get a PADI Open Water diving certification (~9,000–10,000 THB for a 3-day course). If budget allows, this is a great place to learn to dive. Snorkeling is also excellent and free from many beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget snorkeling boat tour around Koh Tao's best snorkeling spots — Shark Bay (Ao Leuk), Japanese Gardens, and Hin Wong Bay (~300–500 THB for a shared tour). Spot blacktip reef sharks, turtles, and colorful reef fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to the John-Suwan Rock Viewpoint — a 30-minute uphill hike through the jungle to a massive boulder with stunning 360-degree views over Koh Tao, Koh Nang Yuan, and the Gulf of Thailand (free). Visit the tiny and beautiful Koh Nang Yuan island just off Koh Tao (~100 THB entry by longtail boat).
day_by_day.afternoon_extra: Swim at Koh Nang Yuan's famous split beach — a sandbar connecting three tiny islands.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sairee Beach for a final island evening. Watch the fire show performances that happen on the beach strip most evenings (free). Enjoy a seafood dinner and fresh coconut.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl and coffee at a Sairee Beach cafe (~120 THB)
meals.lunch: Beach shack lunch on Koh Nang Yuan or packed snacks (~150 THB)
meals.dinner: Sairee Beach — grilled whole fish with garlic and lime, jasmine rice, and papaya salad (~220 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Nang Yuan has a strict no plastic bottles policy — bring a reusable water bottle. The John-Suwan viewpoint is best done in the morning before it gets too hot. Book any diving activities the evening before to get an early start.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise swim or snorkel from Sairee Beach. Pack your bags and grab a final Thai breakfast. Do a last-minute souvenir shopping at the local market near Mae Haad pier — pick up dried mango, Thai spices, and handmade jewelry at budget prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the afternoon ferry from Koh Tao back to Surat Thani or Chumphon (~600–700 THB). Connect to a bus or train toward Bangkok if flying home from Suvarnabhumi Airport, or arrange onward transport based on your departure flight. Reflect on an incredible 13 days of Thailand's best beaches, islands, jungles, and street food.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Bangkok or your departure hub. If time allows before your flight, grab a final Thai meal at a local restaurant near the airport. Stock up on Thai snacks at 7-Eleven for the journey home — mango sticky rice, crispy seaweed, and Thai milk tea.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — Khao Niao Mamuang (mango sticky rice) and fresh fruit (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Quick meal at the pier or ferry snack bar (~100 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport area local restaurant or food court — one last bowl of Tom Yum noodles (~120 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: Total estimated daily spend on this trip is approximately 800–1,500 THB/day (~$22–$42 USD) including accommodation, food, transport, and activities — very achievable with smart planning. Always negotiate tuk-tuk and taxi prices before getting in, and use shared transport wherever possible to keep costs down. Thailand is an incredibly rewarding budget destination — enjoy every moment!

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and take a pre-arranged shuttle or taxi to Rassada Pier in Phuket, then board a high-speed ferry to Phi Phi Don Island (approx. 1.5–2 hour journey). Check in to your boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the Tonsai Village waterfront to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tonsai Village's vibrant night scene. Browse the lively walking street lined with local vendors, souvenir shops, and street food stalls. Watch the sunset from the pier area and enjoy the relaxed island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at the airport — grab a light snack or coffee at Phuket International Airport's food court.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite on the ferry or upon arrival at a beachside café in Tonsai Village — try a simple Pad Thai or fresh spring rolls (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Papaya Restaurant in Tonsai Village — a beloved local spot serving authentic Thai dishes like green curry, tom yum soup, and mango sticky rice at mid-range prices (~250–400 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry tickets in advance, especially during October. Keep some Thai Baht cash handy for the ferry and small vendors. October is the tail end of the rainy season on the Andaman coast — expect occasional showers but also fewer crowds and lower prices.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk up to the famous Phi Phi Viewpoint. The hike takes about 20–30 minutes and rewards you with a breathtaking panoramic view of both Tonsai and Loh Dalum Bays. Bring water and wear comfortable shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling tour around Phi Phi's nearby reefs, including Hin Klang and Bida Nok — both known for colorful coral and diverse marine life including reef sharks and turtles. Tours typically run 2–4 hours and cost around 500–800 THB per person.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Loh Dalum Bay beach for a relaxed evening. Rent a beach chair, sip a fresh coconut, and watch the famous Phi Phi fire show performances that light up the beach after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — try a Thai-style breakfast of khao tom (rice soup) with egg and fresh fruit (~100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Pack a snack for the snorkeling trip or grab lunch at a beachside shack near Loh Dalum — fresh grilled fish or a green mango salad (~200–300 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant in Tonsai — a popular mid-range spot known for its massaman curry, seafood dishes, and friendly atmosphere (~300–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: The viewpoint can be slippery after rain — wear grip shoes. Book snorkeling tours the evening before at any of the many tour kiosks in Tonsai Village. Sunscreen and reef-safe products are strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat to Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh — the iconic beach made famous by the movie 'The Beach.' The bay has restricted access and timed entry slots, so book in advance. Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy the stunning turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your island-hopping with a stop at Pileh Lagoon, a stunning emerald-green enclosed lagoon on Phi Phi Leh, perfect for swimming and photography. Then head to Viking Cave to see ancient cliff paintings and the famous swallow nests.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Spend the evening wandering the street food alleys of Tonsai Village, sampling local bites and picking up handmade souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a local bakery — banana pancakes with honey are a Thai island staple (~80–120 THB).
meals.lunch: Bring packed snacks and water for the boat tour, or enjoy a simple lunch at a floating restaurant near Maya Bay area if available.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner in Tonsai — try satay skewers, pad see ew, grilled corn, and mango sticky rice from various stalls (~150–250 THB total for a satisfying spread).

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has strict visitor limits and specific entry times — book your longtail boat tour the day before. Swimming is allowed in designated zones only. Bring waterproof bags for cameras and phones.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning kayaking around the limestone cliffs and hidden coves of Phi Phi Don. Rent a kayak from the beach (~200–300 THB/hour) and explore at your own pace, discovering small sea caves and quiet lagoons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Phi Phi to Ao Nang in Krabi Province (approx. 1.5 hours, ~350–500 THB). Check in if you have accommodation there, or simply use it as a base. Visit the Ao Nang beachfront and take a longtail boat to Railay Beach, one of Thailand's most dramatic beaches accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Railay Beach at sunset — walk between Railay West and Railay East, and climb up to the Railay Viewpoint for a stunning panorama. Return to Ao Nang for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Phi Phi boutique hotel before checkout — request an early meal if needed.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Ao Nang upon arrival — try a local restaurant on the strip for khao pad (fried rice) with seafood (~150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Krua Thara Restaurant in Ao Nang — a well-regarded local restaurant with fresh seafood and traditional Thai curries with beautiful bay views (~300–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel day between islands. Keep luggage manageable for ferry and longtail boat transfers. Railay Beach longtail boats run frequently from Ao Nang pier (~100 THB each way). The beach is stunning even in October.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island-hopping tour from Ao Nang or Krabi to the 4 Islands — Koh Mook, Koh Kradan, Koh Libong, and Koh Cheuk. Morning highlights include snorkeling at crystal-clear reefs and exploring the famous Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot) on Koh Mook, accessible only by swimming through a dark tunnel that opens to a hidden beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the 4 Islands tour — relax on the white sands of Koh Kradan, snorkel among colorful fish, and enjoy a buffet lunch typically included in tour packages. The tour returns to the mainland by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Ao Nang, enjoy a leisurely evening walk along the beach promenade. Browse the night market for souvenirs and street food snacks.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your accommodation before the tour departs (~7:00–8:00 AM).
meals.lunch: Buffet lunch included in the 4 Islands tour package, typically served on one of the islands (~Thai staples, fresh fruit, water).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a street food market in Ao Nang — try boat noodles, fresh oysters, and coconut ice cream (~200–300 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Book the 4 Islands tour the evening before from any tour operator in Ao Nang (~1,200–1,800 THB per person including lunch and snorkeling gear). Bring motion sickness tablets if needed. October weather may bring short rain showers but tours typically still run.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning longtail boat back to Railay Beach and hike to the Diamond Cave (Tham Phra Nang) to see stunning stalactite and stalagmite formations. Then explore the iconic Princess Cave (Tham Phra Nang) on Phra Nang Beach, one of the most beautiful beaches in Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing lesson on Railay's famous limestone karsts — Railay is one of Southeast Asia's premier climbing destinations. Several operators offer beginner half-day sessions (~1,200–1,800 THB including equipment and instruction). Even beginners can scale impressive walls with stunning sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Railay West Beach — one of the most picturesque sunsets in Krabi. Return to Ao Nang by longtail boat for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near Ao Nang pier before heading to Railay — try a Western-Thai fusion breakfast of toast, eggs, and fresh juice (~120–180 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside restaurant on Railay West — fresh seafood platter or a simple Thai curry (~250–350 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Last Fisherman Bar in Ao Nang — a charming mid-range restaurant known for its fresh catch of the day and relaxed atmosphere (~300–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is only accessible by longtail boat from Ao Nang (~15 minutes, 100 THB each way). Phra Nang Beach is considered one of the world's most beautiful — don't miss it. Rock climbing operators include King Climbers and Basecamp Tonsai.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Koh Lanta — take a ferry or speedboat from Krabi (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Koh Lanta is known for its long, uncrowded beaches and laid-back atmosphere. Head to Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) and rent a scooter to explore the island at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ride south along Koh Lanta's west coast, stopping at Klong Nin Beach and the dramatic Mu Ko Lanta National Park. Hike to the lighthouse at the southern tip for panoramic views of the Andaman Sea. Visit the charming Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) with its stilted wooden shophouses and Chinese-Portuguese architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Koh Lanta's Old Town before taking the evening ferry back to Krabi or Ao Nang.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before the ferry at your Ao Nang accommodation or a nearby bakery.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside restaurant on Long Beach — try a fresh fish BBQ or massaman curry with roti (~200–350 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Old Town restaurant in Koh Lanta — try the local specialty of Moo Hong (braised pork belly) or fresh grilled prawns (~250–400 THB) before catching the evening ferry.

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental on Koh Lanta costs around 200–300 THB/day — bring your license. Ferry schedules vary; confirm return times with your tour operator. The Old Town is a UNESCO-recognized heritage area — worth spending at least an hour exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning transfer from Krabi/Ao Nang to Krabi Town (30 minutes by shared minivan or taxi). Visit Krabi Town's famous weekend market or the Chao Fah Pier area. Explore Wat Tham Seua (Tiger Cave Temple) — climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for a stunning 360-degree view of Krabi Province.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Krabi Town mangrove forest by kayak — a peaceful paddle through winding waterways surrounded by lush mangroves, home to monkeys, birds, and mudskippers. Tours depart from Chao Fah Pier (~400–600 THB for 2 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's vibrant Chao Fah Night Market — one of the best street food markets in southern Thailand. Sample local Krabi specialties and mingle with locals.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Krabi Town at a local coffee shop — try khanom jeen (rice noodles with curry sauce), a southern Thai breakfast staple (~80–120 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tiger Cave Temple — simple rice and curry at a local shophouse (~100–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Feast at Chao Fah Night Market — try grilled seafood, southern Thai curries, fresh fruit smoothies, and local desserts (~200–350 THB for a full spread).

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The best time to climb is early morning or late afternoon to avoid heat. The night market runs Thursday–Sunday; check local listings for October schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry or speedboat from Krabi to Koh Samui (approx. 3–4 hours via Surat Thani, or a direct speedboat). Check in to your accommodation on Koh Samui. Head to Chaweng Beach — the island's most famous beach — for a first look.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chaweng Beach and the surrounding area. Rent a scooter or take a songthaew (shared taxi truck) to visit the iconic Big Buddha Temple (Wat Phra Yai) on the northeastern coast — a 12-meter golden Buddha statue sitting on a small island connected by a causeway.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll Chaweng's vibrant Walking Street for street food, shopping, and live music. Koh Samui's nightlife is lively but you can enjoy it at a relaxed, mid-range level.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi accommodation before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the ferry or upon arrival in Koh Samui — try a local restaurant near the pier for a quick Thai meal (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dining on the Rocks or a similar mid-range beachfront restaurant in Chaweng — fresh seafood BBQ with sea views (~400–600 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry/speedboat transfers from Krabi to Koh Samui in advance. The journey may involve a bus-ferry combination via Surat Thani — allow a full morning/early afternoon for travel. Koh Samui is on the Gulf of Thailand side, which has a different weather pattern from Krabi — October can be wetter here.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day island-hopping tour to Ang Thong Marine National Park — a stunning archipelago of 42 islands with emerald lagoons, white sand beaches, and dramatic limestone formations. Activities include kayaking, snorkeling, and hiking to the famous Talay Nai (inner sea) viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Ang Thong — swim in the saltwater lake at Koh Mae Ko, snorkel at coral reefs, and enjoy a packed lunch on the beach. The park is one of Thailand's most pristine marine environments.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Samui by late afternoon. Relax at your accommodation, then head out for a casual evening at Fisherman's Village in Bophut — a charming area with boutique shops, galleries, and excellent restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before the tour departs (~7:00 AM).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included in the Ang Thong tour package — typically Thai rice dishes and fresh fruit served on the beach.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fisherman's Village — try The Shack for a mid-range meal of fresh seafood pasta or Thai-fusion dishes in a relaxed setting (~350–550 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ang Thong Marine National Park tours cost approximately 1,500–2,000 THB per person including lunch, kayaking, and snorkeling gear. Book through your hotel or a reputable tour operator. The park is closed during rough weather — have a backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Koh Samui to Koh Tao (approx. 2 hours) — one of the world's best destinations for scuba diving and snorkeling. Check in to accommodation and head to Sairee Beach, the main beach, for a morning swim and exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a snorkeling or introductory scuba diving session around Koh Tao's famous dive sites — Shark Bay (Ao Leuk), Japanese Gardens, and Twins are excellent for beginners. Many dive shops offer discover scuba packages (~2,500–3,500 THB) or snorkeling tours (~500–800 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the viewpoint above Sairee Beach, then explore Koh Tao's relaxed village strip for dinner and live acoustic music at a beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the ferry or at a café near Koh Samui pier before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside café on Sairee Beach — try a fresh fish sandwich or Thai green curry (~150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Barracuda Restaurant on Koh Tao — a popular mid-range spot with excellent fresh seafood and Thai dishes (~300–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Koh Tao is renowned as one of the cheapest places in the world to get PADI certified. If interested, a 3–4 day Open Water course costs ~10,000–12,000 THB. For a day visit, snorkeling tours are a great alternative. October seas can be choppy — take seasickness precautions.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Koh Samui by morning ferry. Spend your last full day relaxing and revisiting favorite spots. Visit the Nathon Market in Koh Samui Town for last-minute souvenir shopping and authentic local street food away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage at one of Koh Samui's many reputable spas — a 1-hour traditional massage costs around 300–500 THB. Then visit Lamai Beach for a final swim in the Gulf of Thailand. Explore the quirky Grandmother and Grandfather Rocks (Hin Ta and Hin Yai) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special restaurant. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar, then head for a memorable final Thai meal. Pack your bags and prepare for your departure day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Koh Samui hotel — enjoy a full spread before a relaxed final day.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nathon Market — sample authentic southern Thai dishes like khao yam (rice salad) and gaeng tai pla (fermented fish curry) (~100–200 THB).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The Larder or a similar upscale-casual restaurant in Chaweng or Bophut — splurge slightly for a memorable last meal with fresh seafood and Thai desserts (~500–800 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to recharge before your final departure. Confirm any onward flight or ferry bookings. Pick up last-minute gifts at the Nathon Market — it's more authentic and affordable than tourist shops. Book your Thai massage in advance at a reputable spa.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Samui — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take one last walk on the beach. Depending on your departure time, you may have time for a brief visit to a local café or a final bowl of tom kha soup before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Koh Samui Airport (USM) for your departure flight. Koh Samui has a private airport with direct flights to Bangkok and several international destinations. Alternatively, take a ferry to Surat Thani and connect to Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry wonderful memories of 13 days of Thai beaches, island hopping, and incredible street food. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast at a local café — try khao tom (rice porridge) with condiments, fresh tropical fruit, and Thai iced coffee (~100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick bite near the pier before departure — pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) or a simple noodle soup (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or dinner at Bangkok airport if transiting — grab a final Thai meal at one of the airport's local food stalls.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Koh Samui Airport at least 2 hours before your flight. The airport is small but efficient. Double-check baggage allowances — you may have picked up extra souvenirs! Exchange remaining Thai Baht before departure or at the airport. Keep some cash for airport taxis and tips.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and arrange a premium private transfer to your pier. Board a private longtail boat or speedboat transfer to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to your boutique stay, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink while soaking in the stunning island views from your villa terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Tonsai Village's beachfront promenade for a gentle first-night exploration. Watch the sunset from a cliffside viewpoint or the hotel's private beach. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack or premium bento box arranged by your private transfer service during transit
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique resort's signature restaurant — fresh grilled seafood platter with Thai herbs, jasmine rice, and a chilled glass of Sauvignon Blanc overlooking the Andaman Sea

day_by_day.notes: October is the tail end of the wet season in Krabi — expect occasional short rain showers but generally warm and lush conditions. Pack a light rain jacket. Confirm speedboat transfer 24 hours in advance. Tipping the boat crew is customary.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise yoga session on the resort's private beach or deck. After yoga, enjoy a leisurely premium breakfast. Then embark on a guided snorkeling tour around Phi Phi's famous coral reefs — visit Hin Klang and Hin Bida marine sanctuaries, renowned for leopard sharks and vibrant coral gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Leh — visit the iconic Maya Bay (book timed entry in advance), explore Pileh Lagoon's emerald green waters, and snorkel at Shark Point. Enjoy a fresh fruit and refreshment spread on the boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail hour. Head to Tonsai Village for an authentic Thai street food walk — try pad see ew, grilled satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut ice cream from local vendors.

meals.breakfast: Tropical fruit platter, eggs benedict with smoked salmon, freshly pressed juices, and Thai-style congee at the resort's beachfront breakfast pavilion
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ lunch served on the boat during the Phi Phi Leh tour — grilled prawns, fish, and Som Tum papaya salad
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village street food crawl — budget THB 400–600 per person for a full spread of authentic local bites

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has a daily visitor cap — pre-book your timed entry slot. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only, as chemical sunscreens are banned in Thai marine parks. Wear water shoes for rocky reef areas.

day_by_day.morning: Hike to the Phi Phi Don Viewpoint (Viewpoint 1 and 2) for breathtaking panoramic views over the twin bays of Tonsai and Loh Dalum. The 20–30 minute climb is rewarding — go early to beat the heat. A private guide can be arranged through the resort for a more informative experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking adventure through the sea caves and hidden lagoons of Phi Phi Don's eastern coastline. A private guide will lead you through mangrove channels and into secluded coves inaccessible by larger boats. Return and unwind with a 90-minute traditional Thai massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Thai cooking class hosted on the island — learn to make Tom Kha Gai, Pad Thai, and Mango Sticky Rice under the guidance of a local chef. Dine on your own creations afterward.

meals.breakfast: Khao Tom (Thai rice porridge) with crispy shallots and ginger, fresh tropical fruit, and cold brew coffee at the resort
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at a premium beachside café — grilled fish tacos with Thai basil, fresh lime, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Your own Thai cooking class creations paired with Chang Beer or fresh lemongrass iced tea

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and spa treatment at least one day in advance through the resort concierge. The viewpoint hike involves uneven stone steps — wear sturdy sandals or trail shoes. Carry water.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island hopping excursion via private chartered speedboat — depart early to beat crowds. First stop: Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) for pristine white sand beaches and shallow turquoise waters ideal for swimming and snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for secluded snorkeling among colorful reef fish. Then head to Koh Bida Nok for dramatic limestone cliffs and underwater caves. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch served on the boat with cold beverages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a private beachfront dinner set up by the resort — a romantic candlelit table on the sand with a personalized Thai and international fusion menu and a bottle of champagne.

meals.breakfast: Avocado toast with poached eggs, fresh papaya smoothie bowl, and barista-made coffee at the resort
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the private boat — charcuterie, fresh fruit, Thai rice salad wraps, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner arranged by the resort — 4-course Thai fusion menu: tom yum bisque, green curry with tiger prawns, massaman lamb, and coconut panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Private speedboat charter costs approximately THB 8,000–15,000 for a full day. Request the boat be stocked with snorkeling gear, life vests, and a cooler. Advance notice of 48 hours recommended for the private beachfront dinner setup.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — sleep in or enjoy an early morning swim in the resort's infinity pool. Take a slow breakfast and spend the morning reading or exploring the resort's amenities. Optional: sunrise paddleboard session on the calm morning sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a speedboat transfer to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5 hours). Explore the vibrant Krabi Town Walking Street market and browse local artisan stalls. Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram temple for a cultural experience, then stroll along the Krabi River waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Krabi Town at a premium riverside restaurant. Explore the famous Krabi Night Market for desserts and Thai street snacks before returning by private boat to Phi Phi.

meals.breakfast: Full Thai-Western buffet at the resort — noodle soups, dim sum, pastries, tropical fruits, and custom egg station
meals.lunch: Krabi Town street food — Roti with banana and condensed milk, fresh spring rolls, and grilled pork skewers from market stalls
meals.dinner: Premium riverside dinner in Krabi Town — whole steamed barramundi with lime and chili, stir-fried morning glory, jasmine rice, and fresh coconut pudding for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Krabi Town is a 1–1.5 hour speedboat ride from Phi Phi. Coordinate return boat timing carefully — last speedboat services typically run until 18:00–19:00; confirm with your resort concierge or arrange a private charter for the return.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Railay Beach — one of Thailand's most spectacular beaches, accessible only by boat. Arrive early to enjoy the stunning limestone karst scenery and calm waters. Explore Railay West and Railay East beaches on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing session on Railay's world-famous limestone cliffs — a certified guide can be arranged for beginners or intermediate climbers. Alternatively, explore the hidden Railay Lagoon via a short jungle trek. Swim in the lagoon's serene emerald waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar on Railay before returning to Phi Phi by private longtail boat. Enjoy a quiet dinner at the resort reflecting on the day's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Overnight oats with tropical fruit compote, cold brew coffee, and freshly baked croissants at the resort
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Railay — fresh coconut, grilled corn, pad thai, and fresh-cut fruit from local vendors on the beach
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort — slow-cooked red curry duck with roti, cucumber salad, and sticky rice; finish with fresh mango sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is approximately 30–45 minutes by longtail from Phi Phi via a connecting point. The lagoon trek involves some rope climbing over rocks — wear appropriate footwear and avoid after heavy rain. Rock climbing guides charge approximately THB 1,500–2,500 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Wellness morning — begin with a 60-minute aromatherapy massage at the resort spa followed by a healthy breakfast. Spend the late morning lounging on the private beach or pool with a good book. Optional: guided meditation session offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Underwater photography or PADI Discover Scuba Diving experience at one of Phi Phi's premier dive sites — King Cruiser Wreck or Anemone Reef (boat ride required, approximately 45 minutes). A certified dive instructor will accompany you throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local fisherman for a traditional sunset fishing experience arranged by the resort. Cast lines from a traditional wooden boat as the sun dips below the Andaman horizon. Bring your catch back to the resort chef to be cooked to your specification.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowls, granola with coconut yogurt, and a wellness herbal tea selection at the resort health café
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the dive boat — fresh sandwiches, fruit, and hydration drinks
meals.dinner: Your freshly caught fish prepared by the resort chef — choose from steamed with ginger and soy, grilled with lemongrass butter, or Thai-style fried with tamarind sauce; served with jasmine rice and stir-fried vegetables

day_by_day.notes: PADI Discover Scuba for non-certified divers costs approximately THB 3,500–5,000 per person including equipment rental. Confirm fitness requirements beforehand. The sunset fishing experience should be booked 24 hours ahead through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands by private speedboat transfer to Phuket (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check in to a luxury beachfront hotel in Patong or Surin Beach area. Freshen up and enjoy a late morning swim at your new resort's pool or beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-listed heritage area featuring Sino-Portuguese architecture, colorful shophouses, and vibrant street art. Visit Thalang Road and Soi Romanee for the best photo opportunities. Browse local boutiques for handmade crafts and silk products.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Phuket's acclaimed fine dining restaurants in the Old Town area. Experience modern Thai cuisine with a premium wine pairing in a beautifully restored heritage building.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Phi Phi boutique resort — enjoy it fully before the boat transfer
meals.lunch: Phuket Old Town street food exploration — Hokkien noodles, Oh Tao (oyster omelette), and Mee Sua noodle soup from heritage café stalls
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Phuket Old Town — tasting menu featuring southern Thai cuisine: Massaman oxtail, Gaeng Tai Pla, and Khanom Jeen noodles with coconut milk curry

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private speedboat transfer from Phi Phi to Phuket at least 48 hours in advance. Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot or by tuk-tuk. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Old Town area is generally safe and tourist-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Big Buddha (Phra Phutta Ming Mongkol Akenakkiri) — a 45-meter marble statue perched atop Nakkerd Hill with panoramic views over Phuket island. Dress respectfully (sarongs available at the entrance). Explore the surrounding temple complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kata Noi Beach — one of Phuket's most beautiful and relatively quieter beaches. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying watersports. Arrange a private beach cabana for the ultimate luxury experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise around Phuket's coastline — a private yacht charter with a personal chef, wine, and canapés as you glide past dramatic limestone cliffs and watch the sun set over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast buffet — live cooking stations, international and Thai options, freshly squeezed juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium Kata Noi beach club — fresh ceviche, grilled lobster roll, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Private sunset yacht dinner — champagne on arrival, followed by a 3-course dinner of Thai-marinated grilled seafood, green papaya salad, and chocolate lava cake with coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Big Buddha is free to enter but donations are appreciated. Modest dress is required — shoulders and knees covered. Private yacht charter for sunset cruise costs approximately THB 15,000–30,000 for 2–4 hours depending on boat size. Book 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Phang Nga Bay tour by private luxury speedboat — depart from Phuket's Ao Po Grand Marina. Marvel at the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan) and the towering limestone karst formations of Phang Nga Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the extraordinary sea caves and hongs (hidden lagoons) of Phang Nga Bay by private sea kayak. Visit the floating Muslim fishing village of Koh Panyee for a cultural stop and fresh seafood lunch. Continue kayaking through mangrove tunnels.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket by early evening. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the hotel's spa with a Thai herbal compress massage. Dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the early departure — fresh fruit, yogurt, and energy bars
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at Koh Panyee floating village — steamed crab, grilled squid, and rice served on a traditional wooden platform over the water
meals.dinner: Hotel signature restaurant dinner — Phuket-style Lobster Pad Thai, southern Thai yellow curry with crab, and coconut cream brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay tour departs early (around 08:00) — arrange hotel pickup. The private speedboat and kayaking package costs approximately THB 12,000–20,000 per couple. Wear quick-dry clothing for kayaking. Bring waterproof bags for cameras and phones.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Phuket's Surin Beach and Kamala Beach for a morning of leisure — these are among Phuket's most upscale beach areas. Enjoy a premium beach club experience with sun loungers, pool access, and cocktail service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary — an ethical sanctuary where rescued elephants roam freely. Observe, feed, and learn about these magnificent animals without riding them. A guided educational tour lasts approximately 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Phuket's vibrant Bangla Road in Patong for the famous night market atmosphere. Sample street food, watch Muay Thai boxing at a local stadium, and experience the lively local culture.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — eggs royale, acai bowls, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch at Surin — tuna tartare, grilled tiger prawns with aioli, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Muay Thai dinner show experience — ringside seating with a premium Thai dinner set: green curry, spring rolls, satay, and pad thai

day_by_day.notes: The Phuket Elephant Sanctuary requires advance booking — costs approximately THB 2,500–3,500 per person. Only ethical sanctuaries that do not offer elephant riding should be visited. Wear closed-toe shoes at the sanctuary. Bangla Road is most lively after 21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — final beach morning at Phuket. Enjoy a slow breakfast followed by a last swim in the Andaman Sea. Optional: sunrise paddleboard or morning run along the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium Thai street food tour of Phuket Town with a local food guide — visit wet markets, heritage hawker stalls, and hidden gems. Taste Phuket's unique culinary identity: O-Aew (Phuket iced dessert), Por Pia Tod (fried spring rolls), and Mee Hokkien.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luxury dinner at one of Phuket's top fine dining establishments — a fitting celebration of 12 days of extraordinary experiences in Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Grand final resort breakfast — full spread of Thai and international favorites, fresh tropical fruit platter, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Phuket Town street food tour — multiple tastings across 8–10 stops including savory snacks, noodles, and local desserts
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Michelin-recommended Phuket restaurant — 7-course tasting menu with wine pairing: highlights include blue swimmer crab bisque, wagyu beef massaman, and gold leaf mango sticky rice

day_by_day.notes: The street food tour costs approximately THB 1,500–2,500 per person including all tastings. Book the farewell dinner at least 3 days in advance as top restaurants fill up quickly. Consider purchasing local souvenirs — batik fabrics, Thai silk scarves, and artisan ceramics make excellent gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — check out of the hotel. Depending on flight time, enjoy a last Thai breakfast at a local café near the hotel. Visit a nearby market for any last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Phuket International Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights. Relax in the airport's premium lounge before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry with you the extraordinary memories of 13 days exploring Thailand's finest beaches, islands, and culinary delights.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — Jok (rice porridge) with century egg and ginger, fried dough sticks (Patongo), and Thai iced tea at a local heritage café
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport premium lounge or a quick stop at a quality airport restaurant — Tom Kha soup and a fresh fruit platter
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or post-arrival meal

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer the night before. Phuket International Airport is approximately 30–45 minutes from central Phuket — allow extra time during peak hours. Duty-free shopping at Phuket Airport is excellent for Thai spirits, chocolates, and cosmetics. Ensure all Thai Baht is exchanged before departure or kept as a souvenir — unused currency can be exchanged at the airport.
